gaps.sentence: The children were excited ___ the circus.
gaps.explanation: 'Excited to see' — the to-infinitive follows the adjective.

gaps.sentence: I can't wait ___ you the photos.
gaps.explanation: can't wait + to-infinitive: can't wait to show.

gaps.sentence: This new timetable will mean ___ earlier trains.

gaps.explanation: seem/appear take the to-infinitive: seems to know.

gaps.sentence: There's no point ___ about it now.
gaps.explanation: there's no point + -ing: no point worrying.

gaps.sentence: After introducing herself, she went on ___ the main findings.
gaps.hint: move on to a new activity
gaps.explanation: go on + to-infinitive = do something after finishing something else.
bother + -ing (or to-infinitive): don't bother going. Both accepted.

gaps.sentence: They managed ___ the deadline despite the strike.
